newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares finish lower, U.S. data in focus.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares finish lower, U.S. data in focus.

text.p: Danish share prices finished lower on Thursday after a succession of record high closes, with dealers seeing upcoming U.S. data as determining the market's movement ahead of the weekend but unsure of the outlook.
"It is very difficult to see how the week will end but tomorrow afternoon's U.S. December unemployment data will decide that," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index closed 0.35 point lower at 138.68 in overall bourse turnover of 1.256 billion crowns. The KFX March future fell 0.65 point to 139.60 with 20 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

East Asiatic closed three crowns higher, still benefiting from the announcement of a divestment of its shipping activities to Norway's Tschudi & Eitzen. Leading banks were mixed with Den Danske shedding two crowns to 476 and rival Unidanmark putting on three to end the day at 327.
Otherwise Novo Nordisk fell seven crowns to 537 and ISS, Carlsberg and Danisco all suffered setbacks, while Sophus Berendsen and Moeller's D/S 1912 and D/S Svendborg closed higher.
